Apple has been developing AirPods equipped with cameras, with "Visual Intelligence" as the core feature of this product. The product was initially rumoured to launch this year, but was later delayed until next year.

However, a new possibility has emerged that we may see the first batch of AirPods with cameras this year. Here's why.

When news of AirPods with cameras first circulated, it referred to one version: the internal codename B798. That version is still expected to launch in 2027, and is likely to be a more advanced model.

However, there is another version, called B790, which may launch later this year. Excerpt from the Power On newsletter:

For years, Apple has been developing the camera-equipped AirPods under the internal codename B798. As I previously reported, the device was originally scheduled for launch in 2026, then pushed back to 2027. However, Apple has also been developing another version under a different codename B790 (as is well known, Apple internally develops multiple competing versions of the same product simultaneously). Development of the B790 device appears to be further along: relevant code references have already appeared in internal iOS 27 code, and it has already been placed on Apple's internal timeline for launch as early as this year.

This is not the first time we have heard news of the B790 version. Last month, developer Sam Henri Gold discovered related references in the iOS 27 beta 2 code.

What these products will ultimately look like when they actually come out remains to be seen depending on timing, but there is a good chance we may see the first batch of AirPods with cameras as early as September. What the differences between the B790 and B798 versions are, and whether both versions will eventually reach the market, remain unclear at this point.

Earlier reports had indicated that to accommodate the built-in camera, the stem of the AirPods with cameras would be slightly longer than the AirPods Pro, and would feature an LED light that illuminates when data is being uploaded to the cloud.
